title: How it works

title: Sensor configuration
proposed_content: Body: MPU-6050 at I2C address 0x68, 400 kHz. ACCEL_CONFIG (0x1C) +/-8 g, written as 0x10 (4096 LSB/g). GYRO_CONFIG (0x1B) +/-500 dps, written as 0x08 (65.5 LSB/dps). SMPLRT_DIV and DLPF (0x19, 0x1A): 100 Hz sample rate with a low-pass filter. INT_ENABLE and INT_PIN (0x38, 0x37): motion interrupt as the sleep wake source. PWR_MGMT_1 (0x6B): PLL on X gyro. Register map per InvenSense RM-MPU-6000A. Sketch also sets motion threshold 4 and duration 1 (0x1F, 0x20). trigger: "-". response: "-". Status: open.

title: Firmware state machine
proposed_content: Body: BOOT -> CALIBRATE (gravity vector) -> IDLE (sleep, interrupt wake) -> ACTIVE_SAMPLE -> CLASSIFY -> DISPATCH (plays the clip, BUSY gate) -> COOLDOWN (3 s) -> IDLE. A cooldown timer prevents gag spam; a state latch prevents double-triggering one journey event. Status: open.

title: Blueprint Rev A: system shape
proposed_content: One Next.js 15 "modular monolith": one repo, one app, one Docker image with two entry points (web and worker). Postgres is the system of record, Redis holds queues and cache, S3 holds media, Caddy is the edge. React 19 server components, App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn components, Prisma, BullMQ, Auth.js v5 magic links, Resend, Stripe. Scale by adding web replicas behind Caddy and worker replicas by queue. "No Kubernetes until >$1M GMV."

title: Blueprint Rev A: security and privacy
proposed_content: Magic-link sign-in, JWT sessions with a role claim; /back-office needs moderator or admin; /claim needs sign-in. Rate limits: Hotline create 10 per IP per hour, /api/board 30 a minute, sign-in 5 per IP per 15 minutes. Every input validated on client and server. Content security policy; signed media links with a 15-minute life; webhook signature check and a replay guard; secrets never in the image. A delete-on-request endpoint removes a person's rows across leads, orders, registrations and claim tickets after exporting them.

title: Blueprint Rev A: deploy, runbook and service levels
proposed_content: Production on one VPS (4 vCPU, 8 GB) or Fly.io machines; compose profile "prod". CI on GitHub Actions: lint, typecheck, database migration on main, image build and push, then pull and restart over ssh. Nightly database dump to S3. Rollback by previous image tag. Targets: 95th-percentile page under 800 ms; no lost webhooks; alert when the worker backlog passes 2 minutes. Fifteen environment variables are listed as the contract.

title: Database schema file (Rev A)
proposed_content: Postgres 16, written for Prisma. Five enums: user_role (fan, moderator, admin); order_source (web, kickstarter, gate_desk, wholesale); order_status (pending, paid, fulfilled, cancelled, refunded); ticket_state (pending_review, approved, rejected); referral_state (pending, verified, rewarded, flagged). Thirteen tables: users, leads, claim_tickets, referrals, units, products, voice_packs, orders, order_items, entitlements, registrations, wholesale_leads, events. Three indexes. Details worth keeping: claim numbers like BC-2026-04811; trauma 1 to 5; referral milestones 0/3/10/25; unit serial "printed on compliance card"; entitlement sources purchase, registration, ks_stretch.

title: Blueprint Rev B: media in Postgres
proposed_content: A media table with the file bytes, a unique sha256 for integrity and de-duplication, and an 8 MB limit. Ticket audio is about 200 KB, images about 150 KB, voice-pack archives 5-15 MB (kept as release media; the database stores a per-clip list). Served from GET /api/media/[id] with range requests, a sha256 ETag and immutable caching, behind Caddy's cache. One database dump is the whole backup. Growth about 35 MB per 10k tickets. No CDN until traffic justifies one.
source_excerpt: Backup story SIMPLIFIES: pg_dump = full restore (no S3 cross-sync).

title: Blueprint Rev B: three uses of vector search
proposed_content: (1) Moderation: flag near-duplicates of approved gags (1024-dimension embeddings, HNSW cosine). (2) Support: answer from a knowledge table before a support macro. (3) Campaigns: search the caption and insult library for past winners to feed social drafts. Embeddings are made in batches by the worker, with a pluggable provider (local bge-large or hosted); if it fails, search falls back to plain text matching.

title: Hotline audio worker: the design decision
proposed_content: The worker does not call a live text-to-speech service. It stitches a clip from a fixed library: 3 intros x 12 locations x 15 insults x 5 trauma-tiered outros, pre-rendered once per voice pack by the contracted voice actor; about 35 files in all. Reasons given: near-zero marginal cost, renders under 2 seconds, no outside service to fail on a viral night.

title: Hotline audio worker: the eight hops
proposed_content: 1. Commit the ticket row, then enqueue after the commit, never inside the transaction. 2. The job id is the claim number, so duplicates collapse into one job. 3. The consumer locks the row and requires render_status = 'pending', so a replay is a no-op. 4. Claim-number parity picks the intro; the wizard choices pick location and insult; the trauma slider (1-5) picks the outro; four files, about 200 KB. 5. Fragments come from a 512 MB disk cache on the worker, filled at boot and checked against a manifest. 6. One ffmpeg pass joins them, normalises loudness (loudnorm I=-16, TP=-1.5) and adds short fades. 7. Upload under the claim number, immutable; a retry overwrites the same key. 8. Mark the row rendered, then send the reveal email and the list event.

title: Hotline audio worker: timing, failure and capacity
proposed_content: The ticket image renders on a faster parallel queue, so the page shows the fake legal document at once and the audio player appears a few seconds later by polling. End to end: 6-9 s cold, 3-4 s warm. Failure: retry at 5 s, 30 s and 3 min; after three failures the job goes to the dead-letter queue with an alert badge in the moderation inbox; a bad fragment file is quarantined in the manifest. Capacity: about 120 renders a minute per worker at concurrency 4, above a 500-concurrent-claim load-test target; add a worker container if it spikes. Watch in the first 48 hours: if everyone picks trauma 5 the top outro wears out; record second and third alternates per tier.
